item.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
item.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.

item.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong
item.description: The Cornell lawsuit filed by a woman alleging a brutal rape raises questions on how police handle such cases. The majority of police lack adequate training on trauma-informed approaches, experts say.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump officials changed forms for overseas voters amid a GOP push to restrict voting
item.description: The Pentagon made last-minute changes to forms that many overseas U.S. citizens use for absentee voting, removing a category of citizens that Republicans have been pushing to block from voting.

item.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
item.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.

item.title: A pilot stabs another pilot and tries to crash their flight to Tel Aviv, Israel says
item.description: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, a passenger and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.

item.title: They were promised protection. Instead, these kids with disabilities died in foster care
item.description: Disabled kids make up the largest group in foster care. They have the worst outcomes. They stay in foster care longest. They're the most likely to die.

item.title: Drugs are widely used to sedate dementia patients. Her sons wanted to keep her off them
item.description: Potent sedating medications are often used on agitated people with dementia in long-term care facilities despite federal efforts to discourage them. A clash over whether to drug a Michigan woman illuminates the wrenching decisions families and guardians face.
